extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent holders, licensees, IP lawyers, patent examiners, and government officials dealing with Indonesian patent law
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying statutory requirements and procedural standards from the Indonesian national patent law (provisions on compulsory licenses, government use, simple patents, fees, invalidation, dispute resolution, interlocutory relief, investigation, prohibited actions, and related timelines). Useful for compliance, advising clients, or preparing filings/litigation in Indonesia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license non-transferability
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License is not transferrable, except due to inheritance. (Article 102(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of inheritance transfer of compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compulsory License is transferred by inheritance, the Ministerial Decision on granting Compulsory License remains in effect to the beneficiary. (Article 102(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The beneficiary must report the transfer to the Minister to be recorded and published; failure to report invalidates the Ministerial Decision (Article 102(3) & (5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting inheritance transfer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License transferred from inheritance must be reported to the Minister to be recorded in the patent database and published in electronic and/or non-electronic media. (Article 102(3))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the beneficiary does not report the transfer as required, the Ministerial Decision on granting the compulsory License is invalid (Article 102(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferee bound to original compulsory license terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory license transferred by inheritance remains bound to the requirements and conditions, particularly on the period, as set out in the decision granting the compulsory License. (Article 102 paragraphs referencing Article 86(4) and Article 88(4))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transferee cannot change the grant's period or conditions; the original granting decision's terms continue to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of compulsory license – expiration or court nullification
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License is terminated because of the expiry of the period set forth in the Minister's decision or due to a decision of the Commercial Court with permanent legal power to nullify the Ministerial Decision regarding the granting of a compulsory License. (Article 103(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial nullification of compulsory license (holder request grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License may be terminated by nullification based on a Ministerial Decision upon request of Patent Holder if: (a) the grounds that formed the basis for granting the compulsory License no longer exist; (b) the compulsory Licensee evidently has not implemented the compulsory License or has not made appropriate preparations for immediate implementation; or (c) the compulsory Licensee is no longer complying with other terms and conditions. (Article 103(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for nullification on grounds of non-implementation (point b) may be carried out after 24 months since the date of decision granting the compulsory License (Article 103(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of other terms/conditions whose breach may justify termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Other terms and conditions which must be complied by the compulsory Licensee may include payment of Remuneration or compliance to the scope of License set forth in the decision to grant a Compulsory License. (Article 103(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of nullification decision timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister is required to notify the decision on nullification of a compulsory License to the Patent Holder (or proxy) and Compulsory Licensee (or proxy). Notification is communicated not later than 14 days from the issuance date of the Ministerial Decision on nullification. (Article 104(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and publication of compulsory license termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister must record the termination of a compulsory License in the Patent database and publish it in electronic and/or non-electronic media not later than 14 days from the date of terminated compulsory License. (Article 105(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of patent holder rights on termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination of a compulsory License results in the restoration of the right of Patent Holder to the relevant Patent as from the date of recording of termination. (Article 106)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent as collateral (fiducia) permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights may be used as collateral object of fiducia. Provisions on terms and conditions to use Patent as collateral object of fiducia are regulated by a Government Regulation. (Article 108(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Government may use a Patent in Indonesia on grounds related to national defense and security; or extreme urgency for the interest of the public. (Article 109(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government use must be restrictive, to satisfy national needs, and non-commercial (Article 109(2)). Government use procedures are regulated by Presidential Regulation and conducted for a definite period which may be extended after hearing relevant ministers/heads of institutions (Article 109(3)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of defense/security technologies for government use
rubrics_metrics.description: Government use for defense/security includes firearms, ammunition, military explosives, interception, wiretapping, surveillance, encrypting device and encryption analysis device, and/or other processes and/or apparatus for defense and security of the State. (Article 110)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of urgent public-interest technologies for government use
rubrics_metrics.description: Government use for urgent public interest includes: (a) pharmaceutical and/or biotechnology products expensive and/or necessary for treating epidemic diseases, diseases causing significant permanent disability, and PHEIC; (b) chemical and/or biotechnology agricultural products needed for food security; (c) veterinary drugs needed to handle pests and endemic animal diseases; (d) processes/products to overcome natural or environmental disaster. (Article 111)

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of government use on patent holder exclusive rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If Government use concerns defense/security, a Patent Holder cannot exercise his/her exclusive right as referred to in Article 19. If Government use is for urgent public interest, it does not prejudice the Patent Holder's right to exercise exclusive rights. (Article 112(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different legal effect depending on the ground of government use: complete suspension of exclusivity for defense/security; not prejudicial for urgent public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-only use where patent disrupts state defense/security interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent deemed to disrupt or contravene State interest on defense and security is only used by the Government. If Government does not intend to self-use such Patent, use is conducted by the Patent Holder only upon Government approval. (Article 113(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Holder of such used Patent is exempted from paying annual fees; Patent Holder who uses Patent upon Government non-self-use is exempted until the Patent is exploited (Article 113(3)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, publication, and finality for government use decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Government must notify the Patent Holder in writing of intent to use (Article 114(1)). A copy of the Presidential Regulation approving Government use is sent by the Minister to the Patent Holder. Government use is recorded and published. A decision to self-exploit a Patent is final and binding. (Article 114(2)-(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for government use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government must provide reasonable Remuneration to the Patent Holder as compensation for Government use of a Patent. (Article 115(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and conditions of third party exploitation on behalf of government
rubrics_metrics.description: If Government is incapable of self-exploiting a Patent, it may appoint a third party to carry out exploitation. The third party must: (a) own facilities and capabilities to implement the relevant Patent; (b) not transfer the implementation of Patent to other parties; and (c) have good methods of production, distribution, and monitoring in accordance with legislation. (Article 116(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third party provides remuneration on behalf of the Government (Article 116(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration dispute and litigation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Patent Holder does not agree with the amount of Remuneration, the Patent Holder may file a lawsuit to the Commercial Court within 90 days from the date a copy of the Presidential Regulation is sent. If the Patent Holder does not file suit, they are deemed to agree. The lawsuit does not cease Government use of the Patent. (Article 117(1)-(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fee exemption for government-used patents depending on ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Holder is exempted from paying annual fee for a Patent used by the Government on defense/security grounds; Patent Holder is required to pay annual fee for a Patent used by the Government on urgent public interest grounds. (Article 118(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for Government use are charged to the State Budget (Article 119).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Patent: single invention limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple Patent is only granted for one Invention. (Article 122(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All provisions of the Law apply mutatis mutandis to simple Patents except specific exceptions (Article 121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Patent substantive examination request timing and fee consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for substantive examination on simple Patent may be submitted with filing or not later than 6 months from the simple Patent Application Filing Date and is subject to fees. If request or fee not submitted within that period, the simple Patent Application is deemed withdrawn. (Article 122(2)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Patent announcement timing and substantive exam sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement of simple Patent Application is carried out not later than 7 days after 3 months from the Filing Date; announcement is carried out for 2 months from the date of announcement; substantive examination is conducted after the expiry of the announcement period. (Article 123(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister decision timeline for simple Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister must decide whether to grant or refuse a simple Patent Application not later than 12 months from the Filing Date. The granted simple Patent is recorded and published and the Minister grants a Certificate of simple Patent to the holder. (Article 124(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent documentation and information service obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister performs Patent documentation and information service and sets up a national system for Patent documentation and information network. (Article 125(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: First annual fee timing and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fee for the first time must be paid not later than 6 months from the date of issuance of Patent certificate. Payment comprises the annual fee for the first year payable from the Filing Date to the year when a Patent is granted plus annual fee for the following year. (Article 126(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent annual fee is due not later than 1 month before the same date of the Filing Date in the following year (Article 126(3)). Exceptions by Government Regulation (Article 126(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy payment of annual fees for non-resident patent holders
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual fee may be paid by the Patent Holder or his/her Proxy. If the Patent Holder does not reside or have permanent domicile in Indonesia, the annual fee must be paid by his/her Proxy in Indonesia. The Proxy notifies the Patent Holder regarding amount and makes payment on behalf of the Patent Holder. (Article 127(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-payment of annual fee results in invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the annual fee has not been paid during the definite period, the Patent is declared to be invalid. (Article 128(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holder may request suspension via a grace period mechanism; such inquiry must be filed not later than 7 days before due date; payment during grace period must be made not later than 12 months from expiry date and is charged 100% of total annual fee payment (Article 128(2)-(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effects and restrictions during unpaid/grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: While annual fee has not been paid within the grace period: (a) Patent Holder may not forbid a third party to commit acts under Article 19 nor license or transfer the Patent; (b) the third party may not commit acts under Article 19; (c) Patent Holder may not file civil or criminal lawsuit. (Article 128(6))

rubrics_metrics.name: State revenue treatment and regulation of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: All incomes received under this Law are State non-tax revenue. The Minister, with approval from the minister administering government affairs in financial field, may use the revenue in accordance with prevailing legislation. Further provisions on fees are regulated by Government Regulation. (Article 129(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for patent invalidation (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent may be invalidated partially or entirely on grounds: (a) a request for invalidation from a Patent Holder approved by the Minister; (b) court decision which invalidates the Patent is final and binding; (c) decision to invalidate by Patent Appeal Commission; (d) Patent Holder does not fulfill obligation to pay annual fees. (Article 130)

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation upon Patent Holder request – procedural constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent invalidation on the grounds of a Patent Holder's request is carried out upon a written request filed to the Minister. Invalidation of partial claim is adjusted without expanding scope. Invalidation is not carried out if the Licensee does not provide written approval appended to the request. Decision is communicated in writing to Patent Holder/Proxy and Licensee/Proxy, recorded and published, and takes effect from date of Minister decision. (Article 131(1)-(6))

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawsuit grounds for invalidation and who may file
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent may be invalidated by lawsuit if: (a) the Patent should not have been granted under Articles 3,4,9; (b) Patent from genetic resources/traditional knowledge does not comply with Article 26; (c) the pertinent Patent is the same as another Patent granted to other party for the same Invention; (d) granting of compulsory License failed to prevent harmful exploitation within 2 years from grant; (e) Patent Holder violates Article 20. Lawsuits for grounds (a)-(b) are filed by third parties; (c) may be filed by Patent Holder or Licensee; (d)-(e) filed by public attorney or party representing national interests. (Article 132(1)-(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-limited invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lawsuit regards only one or several claims or parts of claims, invalidation is granted only with respect to those claims or parts for which invalidation is sued. (Article 133)

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation for non-payment – notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent may be invalidated if Patent Holder does not fulfill annual fee obligation. The Minister is required to notify the Patent Holder within 30 days before a Patent is declared invalid on this ground. Lack of receipt of notification does not prejudice invalidation. (Article 134(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, recording and effects of invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Patent is declared invalid the Minister notifies the Patent Holder and Licensee in writing, records and publishes the invalidation. Patent Holder or Licensee of an invalid Patent is not obligated to pay annual fee. Invalidation removes all legal effects related to the Patent. (Articles 135-137)

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and modification after partial invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless decided otherwise by Commercial Court, an invalid Patent is entirely or partially invalid from the date the order for invalidation is final and binding. If partial claim invalidation occurs, amended claim is modified without expanding scope. (Article 138(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee rights where patent invalidated for identical earlier patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee of an invalid Patent on grounds that another Patent for the same invention was granted continues to be entitled to implement his/her License until expiry stipulated in the License agreement. Licensee does not continue paying Royalty to the invalid Patent Holder. If Patent Holder received whole Royalty, they must return amount in accordance with remaining License period to the entitled Patent Holder. (Article 139(1)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith acquired licenses survive invalidation with conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A License acquired in good faith before filing of invalidation lawsuit remains effective with respect to other Patents, provided the Licensee continues to pay Royalty to the valid Patent Holder in the same amount as previously agreed. (Article 140(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidated patent revival
rubrics_metrics.description: An invalidated Patent cannot be revived unless by decision from the Commercial Court. (Article 141)

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to sue for entitlement to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Party entitled to obtain a Patent under Articles 10–13 may bring a lawsuit to the Commercial Court if the Patent was granted to other parties. (Article 142)

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to sue for damages for infringement and evidentiary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Holder or Licensee is entitled to file a lawsuit for damages in the Commercial Court against any person who deliberately and without authorization performs acts as in Article 19(1). The lawsuit may only be accepted if the product or process is proven to have been produced by using the Patented Invention. (Article 143(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and procedural timelines for lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawsuit is filed to the Commercial Court within the jurisdiction of the defendant's residence/domicile; if a party resides outside Indonesia, filed to Commercial Court of Central Jakarta. Chief Justice determines hearing date not later than 14 days from filing. Examination commences not later than 60 days from filing. Bailiff summons all parties not later than 14 days before first examination. (Article 144(1)-(5))

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof rules in process-infringement cases
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination of lawsuit against a Patented process, the burden of proof lies on the defendant if: (a) a product resulted from the Patented process is a new product; or (b) a product is suspected to be result of Patented process even though sufficient vindication has been displayed and the Patent Holder cannot determine the process used. (Article 145(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commercial Court may order the Patent Holder to deliver a copy of the Patent certificate and prima facie evidence and may order the defendant to prove product does not use the Patented process. The judge must consider defendant's interest in protecting described processes and may close the trial to the public upon request. (Article 145(2)-(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timeline and publication duties for Commercial Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on lawsuit must be made not later than 180 days from filing; decision must be made in publicly open court; copies delivered to absent parties not later than 14 days from decision date; Commercial Court must deliver copy of final invalidation decision to Directorate General of Intellectual Property within 14 days; Minister records and announces verdict after receiving copy. (Article 146(1)-(6))

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal restrictions and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal from Commercial Court decision may only be filed to the Supreme Court. A request for appeal is filed to the Commercial Court which decided the lawsuit not later than 14 days from decision. Appellant must submit brief to clerk not later than 14 days from filing appeal; clerk delivers to defendant within 2 days; defendant submits counter within 14 days; clerk delivers counter to appellant within 7 days; clerk must forward documents to Supreme Court not later than 7 days after period in Article 150(3). Supreme Court sets trial date not later than 7 days from receipt and examines within 60 days. Supreme Court decision made not later than 180 days from receipt; copies of decision delivered to Commercial Court clerk within 7 days; Commercial Court must deliver copies to plaintiff, defendant, and Minister within 7 days. Minister records and announces after receiving copy. (Articles 148-152)

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative dispute resolution and mediation prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may settle disputes through arbitration or alternative dispute settlement in accordance with prevailing legislation. In criminal prosecution against patent infringement, all parties must beforehand take mediation. (Articles 153-154)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory injunction remedies available
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request of a party harmed by implementation of a Patent, the Commercial Court may issue an interlocutory injunction to: (a) prevent entry of products allegedly infringing the Patent and/or rights; (b) secure and prevent elimination of evidence; (c) stop infringement to prevent bigger damage. (Article 155)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to request interlocutory injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must be submitted in writing within the jurisdiction where infringement took place and must supplement: (a) proof of Patent ownership; (b) proof of early indication that Patent infringement has taken place; (c) clear statement concerning goods/documents requested, looked for, gathered, secured for evidence; (d) deposit cash and/or bank guarantee equal to value of products subject to injunction. (Article 156(a)-(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and expedited handling of injunction requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If requirements fulfilled, the clerk registers the request and forwards it to Chief Justice not later than 1x24 (one day). Chief Justice assigns a judge within 2 days. Within 2 days of assignment a judge must decide to grant or refuse. If granted, judge issues interlocutory injunction and notifies affected parties not later than 1x24 hours. (Article 157(1)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timings are strict and expedited; clerk/judge deadlines are measured in days and hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance procedure and judicial review of interlocutory injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: After issuance, Commercial Court summons affected parties within 7 days to seek information. Parties may submit statements/evidence within 7 days of subpoena. Within 30 days of issuance, judge must decide to reaffirm or cancel the injunction. If reaffirmed: cash deposit returned, plaintiff may request compensation or report infringement to police. If cancelled: cash deposit is forwarded to the party affected as compensation. (Article 158(1)-(5))

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil servant investigators and investigation powers in patent criminal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain civil servant investigators (and State Police investigators) are vested with authority to investigate criminal offences in the field of Patent and are authorized to examine reports, examine alleged persons, collect information and evidence, examine bookkeeping/records/documents, search/examine locations, confiscate materials/products resulting from infringement, request expert statements, request assistance to arrest/seize/prevent/repress persons, and terminate investigations where insufficient evidence. (Article 159(1)-(2), (9))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil servant investigators may request police assistance, must inform public prosecutor of initiation, and forward results to public prosecutor through police. (Article 159(3)-(5))

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited acts (substantive infringement acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person without authorization from the Patent Holder is prohibited from: (a) producing, using, selling, importing, renting, handing over, or making available to sell, lease, or hand over patented product; and/or (b) using Patented production process to produce goods or any acts referred to in point (a) in the event of a Patented process. (Article 160(a)-(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalty for deliberate unauthorized acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Person who deliberately and without rights commits one of the acts referred to in Article 160 for a Patent is sentenced to imprisonment for a maximum of 4 years and/or fine for a maximum of Rp1,000,000,000.00. (Article 161)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further criminal provisions continue beyond the chunk, but Article 161 sets maximum penalty for deliberate infringement.
